meta.title: Ondra Install Doctor
meta.description: Install self-check (handbook §8.3): run a ported parsePatchYaml / applyEntryPatches / composeEntries to compute the very entry tree the host would see, then report which bundles get skipped and how many patch warnings there are. It answers a different question than the per-package check: that one asks whether this package will load, this one asks what the whole profile composes into. A package can have a perfect patch file and still never load — the profile never listed it, the bundle cannot be resolved, ondra.bundle is missing, or the patch path is wrong relative to the package directory. All four failures happen outside the package, and none of them print anything beyond one stderr line, so the only symptom is a feature that silently is not there. Three implementation decisions: layers are applied one at a time rather than flattened, which is equivalent but lets every warning carry the layer name it came from, and that layer name is the whole reason this package exists; reports are cached by a content fingerprint with a thirty-second TTL checked on read, so no timer is ever installed; inspect() never throws, folding any failure into an unverifiable verdict plus one finding, because it is called by startup and by the UI and one thrown error gets it switched off for good. Read-only is a hard property: it never edits a profile, never writes disabled, never installs a package and never runs an organ. It deliberately does not guess the profile path — the host resolves that through an install anchor and node_modules hoisting rules this package cannot see, and a copied guess would eventually report success while the host skips the bundle, which is worse than no report at all.
